fov.subtitle: Three steps: tell us your microscope, convert your count between fields and mm² (either way), and see how many fields to count for each tumour.
fov.step1Hint: Look at the eyepiece: it has a number engraved, like "10x/22". The second number (the field number) is all we need.
fov.fieldNumberHint: The second number engraved on the eyepiece (e.g. 10x/21 → 21).
fov.field40Title: With the 40× objective (the one used to count mitoses), each of your fields is:
fov.advancedLabel: My microscope has an intermediate lens, or I measured the field with a micrometer
fov.measuredHint: Measure the field diameter on a 1 mm stage micrometer. The other objectives are derived from it.
fov.tubeFactorHint: Leave at 1× unless the stand has a magnification changer or intermediate lens.
fov.invalid: Enter positive values to compute the fields.
fov.tableLabel: See the table with every magnification
fov.formula: Diameter = field number ÷ (objective × tube factor); area = π·(d/2)². Field counts are rounded to the nearest integer, as in the CAP and WHO tables; the exact value is in parentheses.
fov.step2Hint: Pick the direction and fill in the sentence — the result appears instantly. Counted at the microscope? Convert fields to mm². Counted on the digital slide (telepathology) and the report template asks for "per 10 fields"? Convert mm² to fields.
fov.convEmpty: Fill in how many mitoses you counted and in how many fields.
fov.summary: {{count}} mitoses in {{fields}} fields at {{objective}}× (field Ø {{diameter}} mm, {{fieldArea}} mm²; total area {{area}} mm²) = {{perMm2}} mitoses/mm² ({{per2}} per 2 mm²).
fov.refHint: Older criteria are written as "per 10 HPF" of a specific diameter. This converts your density to that convention.
fov.refResult: Your count corresponds to {{value}} per 10 fields of Ø {{diameter}} mm ({{area}} mm²).
fov.reverseToggle: I have a threshold (e.g. ≥ 4/mm²) — how many mitoses is that in my fields?
fov.reverseHint: Given a criterion per mm² (or per 2, 5, 10 mm²), how many figures that means in the fields you filled in above.
fov.reverseResult: {{value}} per {{unit}} mm² = {{count}} figures in {{fields}} fields at {{objective}}×.
fov.revIntro: On a digital slide the count comes per area (the viewer measures in mm²). Say how many you counted and over what area, and in how many fields of which objective the report template wants the number.
fov.revSentenceArea: mm². I want to report it in
fov.revFieldInfo: Your field at that objective: Ø {{diameter}} mm, {{fieldArea}} mm²; {{fields}} fields cover {{covered}} mm².
fov.revRefTitle: If the template assumes a reference field ("10 HPF" of a fixed diameter):
fov.revEmpty: Fill in how many mitoses you counted and over how many mm².
fov.revSummary: {{count}} mitoses in {{area}} mm² ({{perMm2}} mitoses/mm²) = {{result}} mitoses in {{fields}} fields at {{objective}}× (field Ø {{diameter}} mm, {{fieldArea}} mm²; {{fields}} fields = {{covered}} mm²).
fov.step3Title: How many fields should I count?
fov.step3Hint: Each tumour asks for a different area. Pick the tumour and get the instruction ready for your microscope.
fov.pickEmpty: Pick a tumour above to see the instruction.
fov.divideBig: …then divide the total by {{divisor}} (the report is per {{unit}} mm²)
fov.noDivide: The total is already the value to report (per {{unit}} mm²).
fov.coverInfo: Those fields cover {{covered}} mm²; the protocol asks for {{area}} mm² ({{exact}} exact fields).
fov.breastIntro: Count 10 consecutive fields at the hot spot, with the 40× objective. For your field (Ø {{diameter}} mm, {{area}} mm²), the cut-offs are:
fov.breastUnit: mitoses added up over the 10 fields
fov.breastClamped: Your diameter ({{diameter}} mm) is outside the 0.40–0.69 mm range of the CAP table; the closest row was used — confirm before grading.
fov.reqUndefined: The source does not define the field size, so there is no safe conversion to mm². Record your field diameter when reporting.
fov.reqLegacy: Historical reference — {{label}}: equals {{fields}} fields at {{objective}}× ({{exact}} exact).
fov.disclaimer: Decision-support tool. Check the current protocol before grading; field counts are rounded as in the CAP/WHO tables. Reference: Cree IA et al., Counting mitoses: SI(ze) matters! Mod Pathol 2021;34:1651–1657.

prostate.subtitle: Describe how the specimen was split into cassettes, type what you saw in each, and get volume, weighted Gleason (ISUP), margins, extraprostatic extension and a suggested stage — with the specimen drawn in 3D.
prostate.disclaimer: Decision-support tool. Grading follows the ISUP 2014/2019 rules for prostatectomy (a lower-grade minor pattern ≤ 5% is ignored; a higher-grade pattern ≤ 5% is reported as tertiary). Volume is the mean tumour % per prostatic cassette and assumes cassettes of similar size. Staging is a suggestion: check the current AJCC/CAP criteria before signing out.
prostate.step1Hint: Say how many cassettes there are and group them the way you grossed: each group has a name, a cassette range and where it comes from (side, anterior/posterior, tissue). The direction says where the group starts — a whole lobe runs apex to base (or the reverse), a cone sits only at the apex or only at the base. Save it as a template to reuse.
prostate.step2Title: What did you see in each cassette?
prostate.step2Hint: For each cassette: tumour %, pattern 4 and 5 %, and tick positive margin or extraprostatic extension. Enter jumps to the next field.
prostate.step3Hint: Computed from the cassettes. The text gathers the parameters for you to write the report — it is not the report.

breast.subtitle: Two modules sharing one map: at grossing, describe the specimen, ink the margins, place the lesions and say how you sliced — the specimen comes out in 3D with the text ready. At sign-out, rebuild the map, score cellularity cassette by cassette and get the RCB.
breast.disclaimer: Decision-support tool. RCB follows the published formula (Symmans et al., J Clin Oncol 2007) and the MD Anderson Cancer Center protocol: d1 and d2 are the largest dimensions of the residual tumour bed, %CA the average cancer cellularity across the whole bed (invasive + in situ) and %CIS the in situ fraction. Margin distances come from a block model of the measurements entered; the 3D specimen is schematic. Staging is a suggestion: check the current AJCC/CAP criteria before signing out.

guide.title: Visual cellularity guide (%CA)
guide.hint: compare the microscope field with the diagrams
guide.model: Each circle is a field with 1,000 cells = 100%: one cell = 0.1%, ten cells = 1%. Estimate %CA field by field across the whole tumour bed and average, rounding to the nearest 10% (1% and 5% for sparse beds). The usual mistake is to estimate only in the foci with lots of carcinoma.

macroscopy.subtitle: Every specimen's grossing routine, step by step, organised by system. Pick the system, then the specimen on the bench.
macroscopy.emptySystemBody: The specimens under {{name}} do not have a written routine yet.
macroscopy.keyboardHint: The arrow keys move between steps.
macroscopy.missingTitle: This manual page does not exist
macroscopy.missingBody: The system or specimen you looked for is not in the manual.
macroscopy.footer: The manual's content is being prepared and is the same for every account.

frozen.subtitle: Fill in the specimen while it is on the bench and copy the finished report. Masks write the gross description; Mohs draws the quadrants; the timer counts cold ischemia.
frozen.privacy: The document in progress stays in this browser only, under your account — it survives a refresh but never leaves the device. Saved templates live in your account and sync across devices. The report itself is generated in Portuguese.

cong.title: Intraoperative exam — frozen section
cong.cronHint: Counts until the specimen goes into formalin.
cong.isquemiaManualHint: If nobody pressed the timer, write it here.
cong.isquemiaNota: The report will use the typed time — clear the field to go back to the timer.
cong.clearConfirm: Clear the whole document? The timer is reset too.

email.title: Send by e-mail
email.subject: Subject
email.hint: The report goes in the e-mail body as text. If your app cuts it off (some limit the link size), use Copy body and paste it in.

mohs.title: Mohs surgery
mohs.cronHint: Counts this stage until the specimen goes into formalin.
mohs.casseteHint: Repeat the same number on other parts to send them together in one cassette, or write 5,6 / 5-7 to spread this part over several.
mohs.hint: Click a sector of the drawing to mark tumour at the margin. Rotate the axis on the clock when the cuts are diagonal.
mohs.ampliacoesHint: Mark tumour at a margin of the main specimen to enable re-excisions, or add one manually.
